subject: pathology
title: Crescentic GN, Anti-GBM Disease, and Alport Syndrome Basement Membrane Splitting

steps.tx: Crescents fill Bowman space with fibrin, macrophages, and epithelial proliferation when capillary walls rupture, crescentic glomerulonephritis collapsing filtration within days to weeks without treatment. That emergency pattern is **crescentic glomerulonephritis (rapidly progressive GN)**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Crescents mean kidneys failing in days; biopsy and induction therapy race the scar together.

steps.tx: Anti-GBM disease paints glomerular and alveolar basement membranes with linear IgG against collagen IV alpha three chains, haemoptysis and renal failure as Goodpasture syndrome when lungs join. The linear disease is **anti-GBM (Goodpasture) disease**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: Linear IgG, lung haemorrhage, renal failure: anti-GBM disease earns plasma exchange immediately.

steps.tx: Plasma exchange in anti-GBM disease removes pathogenic antibody while steroids and cyclophosphamide stop production, dialysis dependence at presentation and crescent burden forecasting renal recovery. That urgency defines **plasma exchange in anti-GBM disease**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: Exchange the antibody out today in anti-GBM disease; oliguric dialysis patients rarely recover kidneys.

nodes.label: Urgent biopsy, ANCA and anti-GBM sent

steps.tx: Alport syndrome mutates collagen IV alpha three to five chains, splitting and lamellating basement membranes into basket weave electron microscopy beside haematuria, sensorineural deafness, and lenticonus. That woven membrane is **Alport syndrome basement membrane splitting**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Basket weave basement membrane plus deafness and eye signs name Alport syndrome's collagen failure.

vis.caption: Alport syndrome across kidney, ear, and eye from collagen IV mutation.

steps.tx: X-linked Alport males progress to kidney failure by young adulthood while carrier females haematuria variably, autosomal forms distributing risk differently for genetic counselling. Early RAAS blockade delays progression: **Alport syndrome inheritance and early RAAS therapy**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Start RAAS blockade at microalbuminuria in Alport syndrome; years of filtration are bought cheaply.

steps.tx: Thin basement membrane disease thins glomerular membrane uniformly causing familial benign haematuria, yet overlapping collagen genes with Alport carriers demand longitudinal respect. That overlap counsels **thin basement membrane and Alport carrier continuum**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Thin membranes explain benign family haematuria, but collagen genetics blur into Alport respect.

steps.tx: Rapidly progressive presentation triage never waits for every antibody: oliguria, active sediment, and rising creatinine earn biopsy within days and pulse steroids when infection excluded. That tempo is **rapidly progressive GN emergency pathway**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: In rapidly progressive GN, biopsy in days not weeks; kidneys scar while panels travel.

rows: Still treat lung and systemic disease

steps.tx: Goodpasture antigen exposure by smoking, hydrocarbons, and infection unmasks alveolar collagen to circulating antibody, explaining pulmonary predominance in smokers with anti-GBM disease. That exposure link is **environmental unmasking in anti-GBM lung disease**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further.
steps.say: Smoking opens alveolar membranes to anti-GBM antibody; advise cessation as immunology, not lifestyle garnish.
